keywords.nuance: きっと expresses strong confidence about a likely future event while still being a prediction.
keywords.exampleTranslation: It will surely be sunny tomorrow.

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: きっと is stronger than たぶん. たぶん = maybe, きっと = definitely likely.

questions.hint: The speaker is confident about being able to return.
questions.answer: I will definitely be able to go home tomorrow.

questions.prompt: 彼はきっと来ると思う。
questions.answer: I think he will surely come.

questions.prompt: きっとあなたの役に立つでしょう。
questions.answer: It will surely be useful to you.

productionQuestions.prompt: He will surely call you tonight.
productionQuestions.hint: Predict with confidence using きっと.

referenceAnswers.answer: きっと今夜、彼はあなたに電話する。
今夜はきっと連絡してくるはずです。
referenceAnswers.note: Husoku version still carries equivalent confidence.

productionQuestions.prompt: I’m sure the lesson will be easy.
productionQuestions.hint: Use きっと with confident prediction of ease.

referenceAnswers.answer: きっと、このレッスンは簡単ですよ。
きっと大丈夫、これなら簡単だ。

productionQuestions.prompt: Don’t worry, this train will surely arrive soon.
productionQuestions.hint: Reassuring prediction in context of waiting.

referenceAnswers.answer: 心配しないで。きっともうすぐ電車が到着します。
referenceAnswers.note: Very natural reassurance with きっと.

referenceAnswers.answer: 大丈夫、きっと電車はすぐ来るよ。

productionQuestions.prompt: She will surely pass this level.

referenceAnswers.answer: 彼女はきっとこの級に合格するはずです。
きっと彼女、頑張ってこの級を通る。
